page: Microsoft Azure B8as_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 8 vCPUs distributed across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local ephemeral storage, utilizing network-attached Premium Storage instead, and does not include GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the B8as_v2 primarily within the average middle 50 percent across standard compute and memory metrics. It records a Geekbench single-core score of 1517.0 and a multi-core score of 5147.0, with PassMark CPU score reaching 11935.85. Stress-ng scores reflect 2676.08 for single-core and 10751.93 for multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 515.4 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read blocks, dropping to 55.37 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 32.26 GB/sec for 256 MB writes. While the machine handles static web throughput at 8.6 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 8.21 million ops/sec, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression placed in the lower 25 percent bracket at 35.5 GB/sec, illustrating performance limits under sustained multi-threaded data processing.

The burstable CPU model provides qualitative cost efficiency for systems that do not maintain constant high CPU utilization. Because compute resources operate on a burst model, workloads that require sustained 100 percent core saturation will experience throttling once credit allocations are depleted. This architecture is well suited for development and testing environments, staging servers, web applications with intermittent traffic, light microservices, and distributed in-memory caching tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure B8as_v2 is a general-purpose, burstable virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. It provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no onboard local storage, requiring external Premium Storage, and contains no GPU accelerators. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the B8as_v2 delivers average tier performance across compute and memory workloads, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 5147 and Redis throughput of 8.21 million SET operations per second, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranks in the bottom quartile. The burstable CPU allocation profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for applications with intermittent compute demands, making it a viable configuration for web serving, development environments, and caching layers.
